resources.string: Coconut legacy Device Administrator component preserved for compatibility.

Coconut uses Accessibility to detect when user-selected distracting apps are launched, immediately returning home and posting a status notification. It does not read screen content or collect personal data.
Coconut Local DNS filters domain queries locally on device without external tracking.
Coconut requires the Accessibility Service API to detect when you open applications you have explicitly chosen to block (Snap) and prevent their use.
Observes foreground application transitions (package names) solely to determine if a launched app is on your blocked list.
Coconut NEVER reads your screen content, text, messages, passwords, or personal data. It does not record keystrokes or collect usage history, and zero data leaves your device.
When a blocked app enters the foreground, Coconut performs the Home global action and posts a rate-limited status notification.
